title: Ensemble anomaly detector + stability-window rollout guard for canaries
author: Riley Chen
description: Introduce an ensemble-based anomaly detector for the perf canary pipeline and a conservative 'stability window' rollout guard. Motivation: recent incidents showed single-signal detectors (p95 latency only) lead to noisy blocks and false rollbacks when environmental noise (network jitter, transient region effects) spikes briefly. The new detector aggregates three orthogonal signals (latency distribution shift, p95 variance across regions, and network jitter proxy) using a lightweight ensemble scoring (EWMA + Bayesian vote). To reduce reactive churn we require a configurable stability window (default: 5m sustained score > threshold) before the guard blocks or triggers rollback. This PR includes the detector runtime, controller integration, guard wiring in the canary orchestration, dashboards, synthetic probe changes, unit/integration tests, and a migration plan with staged rollout. The description below summarizes design, implementation, testing, and rollout notes.

review_comments: Anika: Can you clarify how the weights are derived for the ensemble? Recommendation: default to 0.5 latency / 0.3 variance / 0.2 jitter and expose in config. Also request tests around weight edge cases.

Riley: Responded that weights are currently empirically tuned from last 90 days of canary history; exposed as runtime config and added unit tests. Will add a Linear task for long-term automated tuning.

Mateo: Noted potential alert fatigue: suggest an 'escalation window' separate from stability window so short blocks open paged-only after longer sustained failures. Requested docs explaining oncall flow.
Riley: Added escalation window config and updated runbook with oncall flow. Also added a non-paging severity for transient blocks under 15m.
Jules: Verified code style, asked for additional type hints in Python and a short note on cost impact. Approved after CI green and docs updated.
CI: Build passed; e2e had two flakes initially but rerun passed. Tests show ~0.3s extra CPU time in synthetic probe worker under heavy load; considered acceptable.
merge_summary: Squash-merged after resolving review comments and adding runbook. CI green on final run; small test flakes were stabilized by adding deterministic seeds to the harness.
release_notes: Adds an ensemble anomaly detector combining latency shifts, cross-region p95 variance, and a network jitter proxy; introduces a configurable 'stability window' (default 5 minutes) to require sustained signal before blocking a rollout; new dashboards and runbook included. Default guard is enabled for internal perf canaries; admins can tune weights and windows via perf-canary/config/guards.yaml.
